overall_reason: The update changes four update-relevant contracts: (1) auto-leave is now initiated once per joint configuration (edge-triggered, pendingConfIndex advanced to the auto-leave index, nil-Data entry that can never be refused); (2) the leader refuses conf-change proposals that do not fit the joint state (non-leave while joint, leave while not joint); (3) empty-payload proposals are never dropped by the uncommitted-size quota; (4) a pending leadership transfer is aborted when the transferee is demoted, not only removed. The old AutoLeaveAdvance demands repeated auto-leave and admits a quota-retry branch, ProposalConfigurationDecisions/OutcomeSoundness demand acceptance (or quota drop) that the new requirement forbids, ConfigurationTransitionSafety is blind to auto-leave entries, and no property observes the transfer/demotion rule. All other properties (including watch-touched ones) still express the needed contract and are kept; several observer fields must be migrated. The old AutoLeaveAdvance eligibility must not be narrowed to the new edge trigger because the new code appears to miss auto-leave for a freshly elected leader whose log is fully applied. Executed evidence (TLC on the actual old/proposed definitions over model-generated records, plus Go runs of both trees) confirmed every proposed edit; no decision changed. The evidence also confirmed three suspected implementation defects that the proposed suite keeps visible.

updated_behaviors_already_covered.covered_by: Go G4 a/b: old code panics on apply, new code does not; NoUnexpectedFatal flags the remaining D3 path (EV-D3)

suspected_defects: D1 (new code, confirmed in Go G2 and TLC WA1): a leader elected in an auto-leave joint config with applied == lastIndex never auto-leaves (oldApplied < pendingConfIndex is false forever); the old code did leave. Flagged by AutoLeaveAdvance (old and proposed).

D2a (both revisions, confirmed G6/WA5): Advance of the committed auto-leave before ApplyConfChange appends a second leave, and applying it panics 'can't leave a non-joint config'. Only the proposed AutoLeaveAdvance flags it.

D2b (new code only, confirmed G7/WA6): Advance of the entering entry before ApplyConfChange misses the edge; the leader never auto-leaves (old code recovered at the next Advance). Flagged by AutoLeaveAdvance (old and proposed).

D3 (both revisions, confirmed G4d/WD3): admission treats a ConfChangeV2 with zero Changes as leave-joint, so ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointExplicit} is admitted while joint and panics 'config is already joint' at apply. Flagged by NoUnexpectedFatal.
D4 (doc): raft.go:1609 'Configuration changes are never refused.' holds only for empty-payload entries.
Retained pre-existing: JointSnapshotMemberAcceptance outgoing-only recipient; CampaignContract counts V2 pending entries while numOfPendingConf counts only EntryConfChange.
unresolved_obligations: U1: whether Advance before ApplyConfChange of a committed conf change is a supported caller pattern (node.go:162-167 allows Advance during application in general). Decides whether D2a/D2b are library defects; the property is not weakened meanwhile.
U2: PendingTransferVoter is scoped to promotable leaders; a leader that removed/demoted itself returns early in switchToConfig (raft.go:1537-1547, untested TODO).
U3 (resolved): encoded size of the nil-Data auto-leave entry measured as 6 bytes.

U4: whether the admission rule should use raftpb LeaveJoint() (zero Transition) instead of 'no Changes' (D3). The proposed ProposalConfigurationDecisions keeps the emptiness rule as an impl-abstraction clause.

U5: reachable-state model checking of the proposed suite was inconclusive (auto-leave states not reached by bounded BFS or random simulation within the time caps, EV-HUNT); the per-edit evidence relies on TLC-evaluated witnesses built with the actual model operators and on Go runs.
